newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh floods kill 25, thousands homeless.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh floods kill 25, thousands homeless.

text.p: Floods caused by torrential rains have killed at least 25 people in southeast Bangladesh, police and officials said on Friday.
They said at least 30 people were injured, hundreds could be missing and tens of thousands were made homeless in Chittagong, Cox's Bazar and the nearby hill districts.
Unofficial sources put the death toll at nearly 40. "Most
of the victims died in mudslides and a few were swept away by torrents of floodwater," one government official in Chittagong said.
"The death toll may go up as it is still raining heavily. Communications with many areas have been cut off," he said.
The flooding has hit areas of the country still recovering from a severe cyclone on May 19 that killed more than 100 people and injured thousands.
Major rivers in the southeast have burst their banks and rivers in other areas were rising fast, meteorology officials said on Friday.
Unless the rain stopped in the next 24 hours, much of the country would be inundated, one official said.

Two of the confirmed deaths were reported on Thursday. One child died after being swept away by floodwater in Cox's Bazar district and an 18-year-old man drowned while trying to get hold of a floating tree.
Of the 23 deaths reported on Friday, 13 died in Rangamati town in Chittagong Hill Tracts, where tribal rebels have been fighting for autonomy for the past 23 years.
"The victims perished under tonnes of mud sliding from the hills, which destroyed their houses," one local official told reporters.
Road links between Chittagong and neighbouring districts, including Cox's Bazar, have become impassable as floodwater washed away several small bridges and partly inundated highways.

Train communications at several sections of the affected areas were disrupted because tracks were flooded or under threat, said Farhad Reja, General Manager of Bangladesh eastern railway. Handling of cargo at Chittagong port was hampered, port officials said. The national airline Bangladesh Biman said flights to and from Chittagong were delayed or suspended.

At least 300,000 acres (120,000 hectares) of crop-land have been inundated, agriculture officials said, but they could not immediately provide loss estimates. Weather officials said they recorded nearly 350 millimetres (14 inches) of rain in the southeastern region over the past three days, and more downpours were expected.
"However, we expect the intensity (of rainfall) to drop by early Saturday," one official said.
Rain has also hit the Bangladesh capital Dhaka and large areas in the northeastern tea-growing district of Sylhet, local officials said.
